newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish publishers concerned over Ruch sale delay.
newsitem.headline: Polish publishers concerned over Ruch sale delay.

text.p: The Polish press publishers bidding for the newsstand chain Ruch SA in a consortium led by French Hachette Distribution Services said on Thursday they were concerned over a delay in the company's privatisation.

They criticised the treasury ministry in a statement for having suggested that it might begin talks on the sale of a 75-percent-stake in Ruch with another investor, even though it had signed a tentative accord on selling the equity to the Hachette-led group.
"This step can be treated as an attempt at stopping the privatisation of Ruch by questioning...the agreed principle that Hachette has the right to be the sole negotiator," the statement said.

Deputy treasury minister Leszek Juchniewicz said in Thursday's edition of the daily Gazeta Wyborcza that the ministry might annul the deal with Hachette if an offer by a domestic bidder proved better.
He said he might ask the minister to sign an agreement with a Polish consortium, Polska Grupa Kapitalowa, which includes Universal, if its offer to buy Ruch proved better.
"I would do it without qualms," the newspaper quoted Juchniewicz as saying.

On Thursday Universal spokeswoman Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters that her firm received a letter from the ministry asking the consortium, which includes Optimus, cable television operator Polsat and mineral water maker Multico, to make a final offer, which it would likely submit on Friday.
Last month Juchniewicz told a news conference that the ministry was seeking better terms for the deal with Hachette.
He said the ministry's December acceptance of a price offer from the Hachette-led consortium embraced only frame terms of the sale and details still needed to be hammered out.

He said he expected Hachette to spend more and sooner on increasing Ruch's capital and strongly criticised Hachette for unveiling in French and then in Polish newspapers its price offer for Ruch before a final agreement was reached.

The daily Nowa Europa last month quoted Hachette's president Jean-Louis Nachury as saying his company would pay $84 million for a 75 percent stake in Ruch and then earmark a further $45 million for increasing its capital.
Ruch has a 65 percent share of Poland's press distribution market and owns 17,000 news-stands nationwide. Its net profit in 1995 was 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys.
